definition: A geometric derivation mechanism in which a boundary surface is constructed from the centre plane of a wall or other wall-like occupation feature.
altlabel: wall center plane;wall centreline plane;wall mid-plane

definition: A geometric derivation mechanism in which geometry is derived by projecting or extending an existing face onto a required plane, surface, or spatial extent.
A geometric derivation mechanism in which geometry is constructed at a specified distance from an existing reference surface or plane.
A geometric derivation mechanism in which geometry is derived from the intersection of a reference surface with another geometric object, surface, or spatial extent.
A geometric derivation mechanism in which geometry is generated by extending a source geometry vertically between specified elevations, heights, surfaces, or vertical limits.
